observation.visible_scene: A first-person view looking along a shiny metal playground slide. The slide's reflective chute runs from the lower part of the frame toward a flat metal exit at the top-center. A scatter of small plastic balls (red, yellow, blue, green) rests on the chute, with a denser group near the upper section and looser balls in the foreground. The blurred metal side-rail of the slide occupies the right edge. Beyond the slide is a sandy yard with a wooden swing frame at upper-left, a low wooden structure at left, and tree shadows at right.
visible_changes: The viewpoint shifts and tilts gradually across the segment: the right-hand metal rail changes angle and the background sand/structures drift slightly, indicating camera movement along the slide rather than a fixed camera.

Individual balls change position relative to the frame. The large blue ball moves from mid-left toward the center-right and downward over the sequence; a green ball in the lower-left rises through the frame; a yellow ball near the bottom moves toward the lower edge; while the dense cluster on the upper chute stays grouped near the center-top.
Mirror images of the balls appear on the polished slide surface and move with the camera; these are reflections, not separate balls.
No editing cut is visible; the change between frames is continuous.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the camera is held by someone sliding, or how/when the balls began moving; the segment is a temporal crop, so the start and end of any sliding or rolling are not shown.
uncertain_details: The exact direction of camera travel (up vs. down the slide) cannot be confirmed from the background alone.

Part of each ball's apparent motion may be due to camera movement rather than independent rolling; absolute ball trajectories are therefore uncertain, though their relative positions within the frame clearly change.
